title: Three Roller Bottles in a Drawer Box: Support and Removal
seoTitle: Three Roller Bottles in a Drawer Box: Support and Removal | MTT
summary: Plan bottle support, cap clearance and removal access for a three-roller perfume drawer box.
intro: A three-bottle drawer needs controlled bottle support and space for fingers to remove each vial. Measure the assembled bottles and cap diameters, map contact points, then review the loaded insert and sleeve with physical samples. The example layout is an illustration and its final construction depends on the actual products.
cta: Share dimensions, filled weights, artwork, quantity per design and destination with MTT. We can review a sampling brief for orders from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Measure the complete bottle

A bottle drawing can omit the installed cap, label overlap or decoration. Record the longest finished bottle, widest cap or shoulder, base shape and filled weight for every variant. Mark the surface that cannot rub. Ask the bottle supplier for dimensional ranges where available, then give the insert supplier a set of representative samples.
Choose support before shaping the cavity

Support the bottle body at areas approved by its owner. A deep recess can hold a vial visually but hide the only practical grip. Sketch where a finger can enter and where the bottle pivots during removal. Review the card separately so its edge does not trap a bottle or enter the sliding path. Avoid assuming the printed image identifies the insert substrate.
Use the actual sequence

Load the heaviest filled variant first, slide the tray through the sleeve, remove the centre vial and then replace it while neighbouring bottles remain in place. Observe cap movement, contact marks and whether the insert rises with the vial. If the tray binds, compare the insert, tray outside and sleeve opening before changing several dimensions at once.
Define the next sample

Give each sample a revision and record the bottle, insert, sleeve, artwork and card used together. A visual fit review does not validate parcel shipping. Agree the whole packed system and intended distribution route with the shipping team. ISTA describes tests as procedures for packaged products in defined distribution contexts. ISTA test procedures.
Prepare the request

Send dimensions, filled weight, photos of sensitive surfaces, quantities and destination. Ask for a breakdown of shell, insert, card, artwork finishing, sample and freight. Compare alternatives on the same bottle and packing sequence, rather than comparing material names alone.
A fit decision under change

Illustrative scenario. A brand keeps the same vial body but changes to a wider cap after approving the first tray. The cap may be the controlling dimension at the sleeve entrance even if the bottle cavity still supports the body. Place the new capped vial in the approved sample, photograph the highest point and check it through the complete drawer travel. If it contacts the sleeve, record the exact sample revision and ask whether the tray, support height or sleeve opening should change. Check removal again after the chosen adjustment.

title: Three-Vial Drawer Set: Keep the Scent Card in the Right Order
seoTitle: Three-Vial Drawer Set: Keep the Scent Card in the Right Order | MTT
summary: Keep three fragrance vials and their scent card in the intended order during drawer-box packing.
intro: When three similar bottles share a drawer, design the card and packing sequence so the intended scent order remains clear. Mark each vial position, define the reading direction and confirm the card is retained without touching decorated surfaces. Check the complete pack with the actual labels and card stack.
cta: Share dimensions, filled weights, artwork, quantity per design and destination with MTT. We can review a sampling brief for orders from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Start with the sequence

Write the intended scent sequence in a packing brief and show which side of the tray is the front. If each bottle has a different name or colour, compare the filled and labelled products in the proposed position. Leave room for the longest name and any barcode or required label. The illustrated sample artwork is a customizable concept.
Locate the card

Decide if a customer reads the card before or after removing bottles. A separate pocket may keep the card visible, but the open edge needs a removal path and the card should not obstruct the drawer. Measure the complete printed stack including any folded leaflet, not just a single sheet.
Control rotation and substitution

If the bottle must face a particular direction, document how the packer recognises the front. A circular cavity may allow rotation. Compare a shaped support or a packing instruction only after checking the actual geometry and cost. Confirm variants with the brand before substituting a bottle or card; do not infer interchangeability from an identical nominal fill.
Run a pack-out rehearsal

Give the sample and a short photo instruction to someone who did not design it. Time is not a quality target here: record where the person hesitates, reverses a vial or catches the card. Open and close the loaded drawer several times, checking card position and visible marks. Record observations without calling the exercise a transport certification.
Agree the production files

List the approved card version, vial sequence, language, quantities and assembly location. Decide who prints and packs each item and how changes reach the packer. Review the discovery set identification guide for another sequence-control approach. If the card carries a retail barcode, the brand should confirm its intended scanning use and artwork; GS1’s general specifications describe placement and quiet zones.
Build a simple control sheet

For each set, record position number, product name, label or colour, card version and the person responsible for checking the packed set. A packing photograph should show the closed and open orientations and enough of the label to identify each variant. If products are loaded at a separate fulfilment site, confirm the instruction travels with the approved packaging sample. Where identifiers differ by market, the brand should confirm the approved artwork and language before printing.

title: Two Cream Jars in One Gift Box: Insert and Removal Order
seoTitle: Two Cream Jars in One Gift Box: Insert and Removal Order | MTT
summary: Plan support, lid clearance and removal for two different skincare jars in one gift box.
intro: A two-jar presentation needs more than two matching circles. Measure each closed, filled jar, plan where the user grips it and check the neighbouring jar remains seated during removal. Review actual lid clearance, contact surfaces and full shipping configuration on a sample.
cta: Share dimensions, filled weights, artwork, quantity per design and destination with MTT. We can review a sampling brief for orders from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Measure the largest finished outline

Measure the closed jars including lids, label overlaps and any tamper component supplied by the brand. Record maximum diameter, assembled height, base profile and filled weight for each jar. Ask which decorated surfaces can touch the insert. A larger lid can control pocket width even when the jar body is narrower.
Allocate a grip for each position

Place the heavier jar where the underlying support can carry the filled load. Provide a practical grip that does not require lifting by the lid unless the product owner permits it. Remove the larger jar while the smaller remains seated, then reverse the sequence. Check if a finger recess weakens the narrow partition between pockets.
Compare complete insert structures

A folded paperboard support, shaped pulp or foam option needs a defined grade and support beneath the product. Compare the actual samples under the same loaded removal sequence, finish and outer-box dimensions. A paper-look surface alone does not establish what is underneath. Review the insert material comparison when requesting alternative constructions. Record the material grade and storage conditions with the sample. Iggesund’s handling guidance explains how conditions affect paperboard.
Close and inspect

With both jars and all accessories present, close the lid without forcing it. Look for contact at the highest lid, rubbing on labels and movement in the pockets. Confirm which closure is actually proposed instead of assuming the illustration contains magnets. If the set is shipped, agree the outer shipper and assessment separately.
Make the quotation comparable

Provide a filled jar set, artwork files, quantity per design and destination. Ask for the box, insert, accessory slot, sampling, tooling and freight to be listed separately. A change in jar lid or packaging orientation may require a revised insert and fresh physical review.
Use two jars to define the worst case

Illustrative scenario. The larger jar has a broad lid while the smaller jar is taller. The larger lid may control the width of one pocket, while the taller jar controls the closed height of the set. Place both finished jars in the insert simultaneously and check the lid above each. If an insert is raised to improve access to the small jar, recheck closed height before approving the change. Document the result against the jar and insert revisions used.

title: Cosmetic Spatula in a Gift Box: Pocket Fit and Packing Brief
seoTitle: Cosmetic Spatula in a Gift Box: Pocket Fit and Packing Brief | MTT
summary: Specify spatula pocket fit, protective packaging and packing responsibilities for a skincare set.
intro: A spatula recess needs to retain the actual accessory and let the customer remove it without disturbing the jars. Provide the wrapped accessory, its contact requirements and loading orientation. Check the finished set in a sample and agree which supplier owns hygiene and product-contact decisions.
cta: Share dimensions, filled weights, artwork, quantity per design and destination with MTT. We can review a sampling brief for orders from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Define the supplied accessory

Ask whether the spatula is supplied loose, in a sleeve or in another protective pack. Measure its full length, widest point, thickness and wrapper. Identify which surfaces may touch the packaging. Packaging geometry alone does not establish cleanliness, product compatibility or regulatory compliance.
Design retention and a grip

A recess that shows the spatula may look neat but make it difficult to lift. Provide a finger relief or another agreed removal method and test it with the exact accessory. Keep the spatula from crossing a jar rim when the box closes. If a wrapper is required, allow for the complete wrapped envelope rather than the bare spatula.
Set the order of packing

Write who supplies and loads the spatula, whether it arrives wrapped, and which version belongs to each set. Rehearse loading with both jars already in position. Check if the packer can see that the accessory is present without removing it. Use clear version labels for the insert and packing instruction.
Inspect the loaded sample

Close and reopen the complete set. Record whether the accessory shifts, touches a decorated lid or catches on the liner. If a pocket changes, check the space underneath and any adjacent support. Sample photographs should show the complete assembly and revision, not imply a confirmed production run. If the complete set will enter distribution, agree a test scope with the responsible shipper; ISTA lists test procedures for different distribution situations.
Coordinate the brief

The brand or responsible product supplier should specify hygiene and product-contact requirements. Share those requirements, the physical accessory and intended packing environment before requesting a sample. Itemize the box, insert, accessory and assembly responsibility in the quotation.
Decide what changes when the accessory changes

Illustrative scenario. A brand changes from an unwrapped spatula to a sleeve after a box sample has been approved. The wrapped piece may need a wider opening or a different finger recess even if its rigid length is unchanged. Place the complete supplied accessory into the sample, check the sleeve edge does not catch and close the box with both jars present. Record who approves the wrapper and contact surfaces, then issue a revised packing instruction if needed.

title: Drawer Gift Box Sleeve Fit: What to Check With the Filled Set
seoTitle: Drawer Gift Box Sleeve Fit: What to Check With the Filled Set | MTT
summary: Review sleeve opening, loaded tray movement and ribbon pull on a drawer-box sample.
intro: Drawer fit is a relationship among sleeve opening, tray outside dimensions, insert and actual product load. Test the filled sample through its normal opening and removal sequence. Record where it catches before changing the structure, and review the shipping pack as a separate decision.
cta: Share dimensions, filled weights, artwork, quantity per design and destination with MTT. We can review a sampling brief for orders from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Measure both mating parts

Record the finished tray outside width, depth and height as well as the sleeve opening after wrapping. Add the loaded insert, card and intended product. Paper wraps, adhesive and an insert that stands proud can affect contact; nominal internal dimensions do not reveal every interface.
Locate the first contact

Open the filled drawer slowly and mark where resistance starts: at the sleeve mouth, one tray corner, the insert or the ribbon attachment. Compare the empty tray with the loaded one. If resistance changes only when loaded, investigate the insert and loaded tray rather than immediately reducing the sleeve dimensions.
Review pull and customer handling

Check the pull direction and whether the ribbon or tab remains accessible. Ask a person unfamiliar with the box to open it while supporting the sleeve. Observe any exposed bottle or card movement, then repeat removal and replacement. Record the actual sample and avoid extrapolating to a universal clearance or force.
Control manufacturing variables

Specify the exact paper, board and finishing stack on the approved sample. A change to wrap, lining, insert or supplier can change the assembled relationship and should prompt a fit review. Iggesund notes that temperature and humidity conditions can influence paperboard handling and properties. Iggesund paperboard handling guidance.
Separate fit from distribution

A smooth drawer on the desk shows only the observed handling result. For carrier distribution, identify product, complete outer pack, destination and test requirements with the responsible shipper or laboratory. Include the approved revision and loaded sample in the quotation brief.
Compare two sample revisions

Illustrative scenario. A loaded tray slides smoothly when empty but catches near the middle when the insert is fitted. Mark the position without forcing the pull. Remove the insert and inspect its edge and tray wall, then compare the corresponding area in a second sample. Change one suspected interface and repeat with the same filled products. Record both sample revisions, the insertion direction and where resistance begins so the supplier can reproduce the observation.
